title: Senior Product Designer - Growth/Website | Deel
description:
Role: Senior Product Designer, Growth/Website
Company: Deel
Location: Remote (Europe, UK, Israel, Brazil)
Job type: Full-time

About Deel 
Deel is an all-in-one payroll and HR platform for global teams. It covers HRIS, payroll, compliance, benefits and equipment for every type of worker in 150+ countries. About 7,000 people work there, fully remote, across more than 100 countries and 74 languages. Deel reached $1B in annual revenue in just over five years and is valued at $17.3B. It’s pre-IPO and growing fast.

About the role 
You’ll join the Website team, which looks after deel.com and every landing page behind it. For most future customers, the website is their first impression of Deel, and this team makes sure that impression turns into a conversation. You’ll be at the centre of Deel’s conversion work: designing, testing and shipping the pages that turn visitors into pipeline. You’ll own tricky, high-stakes problems on Deel’s busiest pages, from the first hypothesis through the A/B test to the shipped design.

What you’ll do 

- Own conversion on the website and landing pages from start to finish. Spot opportunities yourself instead of waiting for a brief.

- Write a clear problem statement and success metric, then design, prototype and launch A/B tests quickly. Keep what works and let go of what doesn’t.

- Bring strong visual and UI craft to every page, and keep each launch on-brand and consistent with the design system.

- Work with growth, performance marketing and sales to understand what the business needs, then turn it into pages that speak to the customer’s real problem rather than internal jargon.

- Use storytelling, in words and visuals, to introduce new products, launches and offers.

- Plan and ship experiments together with growth PMs, engineers, data analysts and lifecycle marketers.

- Design landing pages for new product and feature launches with product marketing.

- Set the bar for craft and careful experimentation, and give other designers thoughtful feedback.

What you need to succeed 

- 8+ years in product design, with a portfolio that shows you owning web design end to end.

- Hands-on experience with CRO, A/B testing and experimentation. You’re comfortable talking about hypotheses, test design, statistical significance and iteration.

- Excellent craft and UI skills. Your portfolio shows polished web and landing page work that actually converts.

- A genuine growth mindset: every launch is a chance to learn something.

- Strong storytelling and a feel for visual hierarchy that guides a visitor toward action.

- You’re at home in analytics and experimentation tools such as Amplitude or GA, and you use both numbers and user insight to make decisions.

- Experience taking a web experiment or launch from idea all the way to design QA.

- You explain your work clearly to designers and to business stakeholders alike.

- Experience building and maintaining a design system for a marketing site.

What you get 

- Direct impact on the first thing most prospects see of Deel.

- Stock grants at a pre-IPO company, depending on your role, employment status and location.

- Fully remote work, plus an optional flexible office membership with IWG.

- A strong design team to learn from.

title: Staff Product Designer - Growth | Deel
description:
Role: Staff Product Designer, Growth
Company: Deel
Location: Fully remote
Job type: Full-time

About Deel 
Deel is an all-in-one payroll and HR platform for global teams. It covers HRIS, payroll, compliance, benefits and equipment for every type of worker in 150+ countries. About 7,000 people work there, fully remote, across more than 100 countries and 74 languages. Deel reached $1B in annual revenue in just over five years and is valued at $17.3B. It’s pre-IPO and leans heavily into AI. Each designer works with about five engineers, and AI has made the team much faster this year.

About the role 
Growth at Deel doesn’t follow a fixed roadmap. The team works from a queue of ideas: lots of CRO experiments and bigger growth bets. On some projects you’ll own the design from start to finish. On others you’ll set the direction and keep the quality high without building a full prototype yourself. Everything you work on ties back to activation, engagement, retention and revenue.

What you’ll do 

- Lead design across growth projects and connect each one to the numbers that matter: activation, engagement, retention and monetisation.

- Design, prototype and A/B test quickly, together with product, engineering, data and marketing.

- Work with the Deel UI team on the design system, including motion, animations and micro-interactions that make growth flows feel good.

- Spot where users or the team get stuck, and fix it.

- Stay close to your engineers from first idea to design QA, and keep the team moving.

- Mentor product designers and help improve how the team works day to day.

What you need to succeed 

- 5–7 years in product design, including 2+ at Staff level.

- Real growth design experience. Onboarding flows, pricing pages, subscriptions or virality features are a great sign.

- Excellent craft, and a portfolio that makes people say “wow”. It needs at least one case study.

- You’re comfortable with experiments and data: you form hypotheses, run A/B tests and show measurable results. Amplitude, Mixpanel or similar tools feel familiar.

- AI is the first tool you reach for, before Figma or a doc. If you have AI work in your portfolio, we’d love to see it.

- You’d rather build than talk about building. You enjoy moving fast and don’t mind figuring things out as you go.

- You communicate clearly and bring people with you, across product, engineering, data and marketing.

Nice to have 

- You can ship your own work to production, for example through the frontend repo, Claude Code or internal tools.

- Personal projects you’re proud of.

What you get 

- High-impact growth work at a pre-IPO company, with stock grants depending on your role and location.

- Fully remote, async-friendly work, plus an optional flexible office membership with IWG.

- A strong design team to learn from, and a clear career ladder.

- Fair pay based on your skills and experience. Deel never asks about your salary history.

title: Langfuse - Senior Software Engineer, SDK
description:
Why SDK Engineering at Langfuse 

Your work will have an outsized impact. 

Our SDKs are downloaded 26M+ times per month. When you ship a new integration or improve SDK performance, thousands of developers benefit the same day — and they'll tell you about it in GitHub issues, on Twitter, and in our community channels. Everything you build is open source (MIT-licensed) and immediately visible.

The SDK is often the very first thing a developer touches when they try Langfuse, so your work directly shapes their first impression.

You will also have direct exposure to how cutting-edge LLM-applications are built. The users you serve are some of the best and most ambitious software engineers in the world and that leverage Langfuse to improve their applications. Deeply understanding the problems they solve will help you design the best possible SDK experience and along the way makes you an expert on LLM engineering yourself.

You will grow at Langfuse by 

- Owning our SDKs . We maintain SDKs in Python and TypeScript both built on OpenTelemetry. You'll be responsible for their reliability, performance, and developer experience. These SDKs run inside our users' production systems, which means they must never fail, must have minimal impact on CPU and memory, and must work flawlessly across every environment — from serverless functions to long-running agent loops. You'll think deeply about the exposed interfaces, error handling, batching, async flushing, and graceful degradation.

- Designing APIs that developers love . How are functions named, how are parameters structured, how are breaking changes communicated, how does the documentation read? Developer experience is a core differentiator for Langfuse and you'll own every detail of it. When we shipped the Python SDK v3 and TypeScript SDK v4 , both were full rewrites on OpenTelemetry — that's the kind of thoughtful, high-impact SDK work you'll lead. Apart from tracing, we also support core workflows of engineers building with LLMs with our SDKs, see our Experiment Runner SDK for example.

- Integrating with every major AI framework : Langfuse integrates with 40+ frameworks and model providers: OpenAI SDK, Vercel AI SDK, AI SDK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Pydantic AI, OpenAI Agents, CrewAI, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, LiveKit, and many more. You'll maintain these integrations, ensure new Langfuse features are supported across all of them, and add new integrations as the ecosystem evolves. When a new framework gains traction, you'll be among the first to instrument it.

- Maintaining our OpenTelemetry endpoint : some users send traces directly to our OTLP endpoint instead of using our SDKs. You'll ensure this path is robust, well-documented, and supports the full range of Langfuse features. This also extends our language support to Java, Go, and any language with an OpenTelemetry SDK. You can work with the OpenTelemetry community to steer the GenAI conventions.

- Writing public documentation : you'll own the SDK docs, integration guides, and migration paths. At Langfuse, docs are part of our core product. When you ship a new SDK version or integration, the docs ship with it.

What we're looking for 

- Strong engineer who gets excited about developer experience, API design, and writing code that runs reliably in other people's production systems

- Experience building or maintaining SDKs, client libraries, or developer tools — ideally in Python and/or TypeScript

- Deep understanding of performance: you know how to profile, benchmark, and minimize CPU/memory overhead in hot paths

- Someone who can manage projects themselves — you know how to develop strong conviction about what to build and how to ship it

- Thoughtful about versioning, backwards compatibility, and migration paths

- Interest in open source software and genuine excitement about talking to developers about their integration challenges

- Thrives in a small, accountable team where your output is visible and matters

- CS or quantitative degree preferred

Bonus points: 

- Experience with OpenTelemetry internals or observability instrumentation 

- Former founder or early startup experience 

- Contributions to popular open source SDKs or developer tools 

- ML/AI background or familiarity with the LLM framework ecosystem 

No candidate checks all boxes. If you feel you are a good fit for this role, please go ahead and apply. 

Learn more about 

- SDK Overview — architecture and design of our Python and TypeScript SDKs

- All Integrations — the full list of frameworks, model providers, and gateways we support

- OpenTelemetry Integration — how we use OTEL as the foundation

- SDK Upgrade Paths — how we think about versioning and breaking changes

- Project you could have built: TypeScript SDK v4 (GA) 

- Project you could have built: Python SDK v3 (GA) 

- Our codebase: GitHub Repository 

- Ben Kuhn on Impact, Agency and Taste 

- Who we are & how we work 

Perks 

- Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

- Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

As Head of Government Affairs & Communications , you'll own and lead SE3's policy, public affairs and communications function. You'll set the strategy that shapes how governments, parliaments, armed forces and the press across Germany and Europe understand SE3, and build the team and relationships that turn that positioning into institutional trust and political standing. title: Senior Product Manager – Digital Clients: Growth & Expansion
description:
Your Role

As Senior Product Manager – Private Wealth (f/m/d) you build the product for LIQID's most demanding clients: entrepreneurs, families and executives whose relationship with us runs through a personal Relationship Manager. You design for two users at once – the client and the RM – and your mandate is twofold: make our Relationship Managers radically more effective, and design the end-to-end hybrid service, sales and relationship model for our most complex offerings. Our private clients hold portfolios that include private equity funds from KKR, EQT, CVC and Permira and venture stakes in companies like SpaceX, OpenAI, Stripe and Anduril. You make sure that advising on, investing in and living with these portfolios feels like the best of private banking – with the speed and clarity of a digital product.

What you'll do

- End-to-End Segment Ownership: Own the private client journey from introduction and first advisory meeting through onboarding, investment and long-term servicing to the next allocation. You define the segment's North Star and KPI tree – net new money, share of wallet, time from advisory to investment, private markets adoption, retention, RM book capacity and cost-to-serve – and develop it further where you see sharper signals.

- RM Enablement & Advisory Tooling: Treat Relationship Managers as users, not stakeholders. You build the tools that give them more time for advice and less for administration: a client 360 view, meeting preparation and follow-up, next-best-action signals, pipeline visibility and AI copilots that draft, summarize and document – within the requirements of MiFID II on suitability, cost transparency and record-keeping.

- Hybrid Service & Sales Design: Blueprint the service model end-to-end: which moments are digital, which are personal, and which are both. Together with RM and Sales leadership you design seamless handovers, a shared view between client app and RM workspace, and service tiers that scale high-touch quality to more clients without diluting it.

- Complex Offerings, Made Simple: Make sophisticated products understandable and executable: private markets with capital calls, distributions and J-curves, and the underlying funds and companies, from Cinven and Advent to Mistral and Databricks, as well as bespoke mandates, company and holding accounts, family structures and consolidated reporting across portfolios. You work closely with the Investment team, Compliance and Operations so every journey is compliant by design.

- Discovery, Data & Experimentation: Join advisory meetings, shadow RMs and run continuous discovery with clients for whom every interaction matters. You combine qualitative depth with rigorous measurement in a small-n, high-value segment, define tracking schemas for client and RM journeys, and use AI-assisted prototyping to converge on solutions in few iteration cycles.

- Thought Leadership with Hands-on Mentality: Act as Product Manager and Product Owner for a cross-functional team of Engineering, Design and Product Ops. You drive adoption of what you ship inside the RM organization, prioritize transparently by impact and effort – which also means saying no – and grow into the thought leader for hybrid wealth management at LIQID.

What you bring

- Background: 7+ years in Product Management, ideally in wealth management, private banking, FinTech or another trust-driven, advice-led domain. Experience building for internal expert users such as advisors, sales or service teams alongside end clients is a strong plus.

- Service Design & Hybrid Thinking: You think in service models, not just screens. You have designed journeys that span people, processes and software, and you know how to drive adoption and behavior change inside an organization, not only ship features to it.

- Domain Depth & Regulatory Fluency: Solid understanding of investing and wealth management (capital markets, private markets, portfolio construction), and the ambition to build regulatory fluency in a supervised environment (MiFID II, BaFin). Experience with private market products or advisory processes is a strong plus.

- Analytical & Technical Fluency: You define metrics before you build and attribute impact credibly, even with small samples. You are comfortable with CRM and workflow integrations, discussing architecture and API trade-offs with engineers, and using AI tooling to prototype and to build AI-assisted workflows.

- Communication & Language: Fluent in German and English , with the presence to earn credibility with experienced Relationship Managers and with clients who expect the highest standard – and to represent your roadmap toward leadership.

- Drive & Motivation: Comfortable in fast-paced, high-ownership scale-up environments. You want to own outcomes, not backlogs, and you are excited to define what a premium hybrid private client experience looks like in an AI-native product organization.

What we offer 

- Diversity : Flat hierarchies and cultural openness make you an integral part of our diverse team of international talents from day one.

- Flexibility : We don’t complicate your life. You’ll find the right balance with flexible work models, working hours, and remote work options. 28 days of vacation and two additional days off on December 24 and 31 ensure you have ample time to unwind.

- Appreciation : You’ll help shape the future of digital wealth management with us in an innovative, multi-award-winning company on a growth trajectory, with high market relevance and plenty of space for your ideas.

- Development : We support your personal and professional growth with an annual development budget up to €1,500. Additionally, at the start of your tenure at LIQID, you’ll receive high-quality equipment, including a MacBook, headphones, and a display.

- Smart Money : As a LIQIDian, you'll enjoy attractive terms for our investment strategies, a monthly lunch allowance, and exclusive discounts with various providers.

- Well-being : Regional organic products keep you fit in the office, and our health initiatives or Health Assistance Program go far beyond that.

What happens next 

An excellent candidate, experience and transparency are our top priorities in the interview process. The different stages help us understand how a potential collaboration could look.

- Initial Call with our Talent Partner : A casual introduction and discussion to align your expectations with the role.

- Video Call with Head of Product : You will learn more about the performance expectations and specific role requirements from our leadership team.

- Take-home Assessment with live Presentation round : A take home task, followed by a 90-minute live session with two team members.

- In-Person Meeting : You will meet some team members onsite, tour our office and sit down with our Head of Product to discuss final alignments.

About us 

We are LIQID, one of the fastest-growing fintechs in Europe. Our purpose is to provide creators, entrepreneurs, and thinkers shaping our future with access to the same opportunities as the world’s most successful investors while balancing the demands of people, planet, and profit.

We offer our clients financial peace of mind through exceptional, curated investment solutions – ranging from the world’s best private equity and venture funds to award-winning wealth management solutions. All delivered via an intuitive digital experience with outstanding personal support. With over €4 billion in assets, we are backed by leading investors from the digital, private equity, and wealth management space, including LGT , Toscafund , HQ Trust , and Project A .

LIQID is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, age, religion, gender, ethnicity, national origin, disability, or any other characteristic protected by equal opportunity laws.

title: Associate Product Manager, Salesforce (6-7 months Maternity Cover)  (all genders)
Product Manager
description:
Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented. 

The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But International Fintechs and non-US banks are left with two unsatisfying options to access it: Either they build on legacy clearing banks that are slow and unreliable, or they interface with middleware providers that don’t move and hold the dollars directly, but themselves rely on underlying legacy banks. Augustus collapses this stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.

We are a group of operators, unicorn early employees, ex-founders and people who walked away from degrees because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and n8n.

We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.

The Role 

You own Banking Experience: the accounts at the center of customer's relationship with the bank, and the API and dashboards they use to manage them.

In this role you’re responsible for redefining what beautiful software in banking looks like. You'll define account structures that give customers powerful building blocks for their products, and craft intuitive interfaces grounded in a deep understanding of their use cases and workflows.

You report to Will, Head of Product, and work closely with Simon, our CTO. You're expected to operate with full autonomy on your team's roadmap, collaborating with design and engineering.

Your First Six Months 

- Months 1-2: Take over day-to-day ownership of the Banking Experience team - the roadmap, the ways of working, the hard decisions. Establish yourself with customers and how they use our accounts. You define and ship your first project.

- Months 3-4: Execution mode. You're unblocking engineering daily, making hard prioritization calls, and shipping your roadmap to customers. You're proactively raising the bar across accounts, API, and dashboard by feeding what you learn from customers into the product.

- Months 5-6: You're working with live customers on the products you've built. Deposits and number of account holders are scaling. You've moved from execution to platform mode - evolving the roadmap based on what our customers are building on top of Augustus.

Who Will Thrive At Augustus 

We believe that throwing smart people with high agency at big problems produces the best outcomes. We’re building a modern correspondent bank, and we win by having a better team. The people who succeed here share the following traits:

- American Dream: You’d rather shoot for gold than settle for mediocrity. You pick the harder goal and stay optimistic when the odds are against you. If it feels easy, we aimed too low.

title: Werkstudent Recruiting (Fitness Trainer) (m/w/d)
description:
Über LIFTED

Mit LIFTED bauen wir die neue Go-to-Marke für Krafttraining auf. In einer Welt voller Longevity Quick Fixes und exklusiver Fitness-Trends konzentrieren wir uns auf einen der wichtigsten Faktoren für ein langes und gesundes Leben: Krafttraining.

Unsere Studios machen Krafttraining einfach, effektiv und messbar – für Menschen, die stärker werden wollen, sich in klassischen Fitnessstudios aber nicht zuhause fühlen. Der Trainingsfortschritt wird digital erfasst, während unsere Trainer jedes Mitglied individuell unterstützen und für ein motivierendes Trainingserlebnis sorgen.

Hinter LIFTED steht ein erfahrenes Founding Team mit tiefem Know-how in der Fitnessbranche & dem Aufbau von Offline Operations. Gemeinsam haben wir BEAT81 von Grund auf aufgebaut und auf 35 Standorte skaliert. Jetzt entwickeln wir Krafttraining mit LIFTED neu – und bauen die nächste große Fitnessmarke auf.

In den vergangenen 18 Monaten haben wir 6 Studios in Berlin eröffnet. Bis Ende 2026 werden wir neun Standorte betreiben. Ab 2027 planen wir, jährlich mehr als 12 neue Studios in deutschen Großstädten zu eröffnen. Um dieses Konzept weiter auszubauen, suchen wir dich als Werkstudent Recruiting (Fitness Trainer) (m/w/d).

Über die Rolle

Unsere TrainerInnen sind das Herz von LIFTED. Sie bringen unseren KundInnnen die Grundlagen des Krafttrainings bei, helfen ihnen dabei Selbstvertrauen aufzubauen und bieten ein einzigartiges Trainingserlebnis. Und genau die Menschen, die das möglich machen, suchen wir.

Als Werkstudent im Trainer Recruiting spielst du eine zentrale Rolle beim Wachstum von LIFTED. Du findest talentierte TrainerInnen, begeisterst sie für uns und begleitest sie vom ersten Kontakt bis zum Tryout im Studio. Mit jedem neuen Studio wächst unser Team – und du gestaltest aktiv mit, wer Teil davon wird. 

Aufgaben

Active Sourcing 
Du findest passende Trainer:innen in ganz Deutschland über Instagram, LinkedIn und andere Kanäle , sprichst sie direkt an und machst sie neugierig auf LIFTED.

Screening 
Du sichtest eingehende Bewerbungen, schätzt ein, wer zu uns passt , und hältst den Überblick über alle Kandidat:innen im Prozess.

Erstgespräche 
Du führst die ersten Interviews , lernst die Kandidat:innen kennen und stellst LIFTED vor.

Tryouts organisieren 
Bevor wir TrainerInnen einstellen, laden wir sie zu einem Tryout ins Studio ein. So lernen wir sie kennen und sehen sie in Action. Du planst diese Tryouts und koordinierst die Termine mit Kandidat:innen und Team.

Prozesse mitgestalten 
Du bringst eigene Ideen ein, wie wir unser Recruiting weiterentwickeln können , z.B. durch sauberes Tracking.

Dein Profil

Du lebst in Berlin und hast Freude daran, Talente für unsere Vision zu begeistern. Folgende Voraussetzungen bringst du mit:

- Studium: Du bist eingeschrieben, idealerweise in BWL, Psychologie, Sportwissenschaften oder Ähnlichem.

- Kommunikation: Du gehst offen auf Menschen zu und fühlst dich auch in Gesprächen mit Fremden wohl.

- Sprachkenntnisse: Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse (jeweils mind. C1-Niveau).

- Menschenkenntnis: Du hast ein gutes Gespür dafür, wer ins Team passt.

- Organisation: Du behältst auch bei vielen Kandidat:innen gleichzeitig den Überblick.

- Eigeninitiative: Du packst an und erledigst Dinge, ohne dass jemand nachfragen muss.

- Fitness-Affinität: Du hast Spaß an Sport – Erfahrung im Krafttraining ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss.

Benefits

- Early Stage: Du bist früh dabei und gestaltest den Aufbau von LIFTED aktiv mit – eng mit einem Gründerteam, das bereits ein erfolgreiches Fitness-Unternehmen skaliert hat.

- Echte Verantwortung: Du übernimmst schnell eigene Aufgaben und siehst direkt, was du bewegst – jede:r Trainer, den/die du findest, steht bald in unseren Studios.

- Learn & Grow: Du lernst Recruiting von Grund auf und bekommst Einblick in den Aufbau eines Startups mit Offline-Produkt.

- Flexibilität: Deine Arbeitszeiten stimmen wir mit deinem Studium ab.

- Berlin HQ: Ein schöner Arbeitsplatz im Herzen des Prenzlauer Bergs (Senefelder Platz).

- Becoming Stronger: Eine kostenlose, unbegrenzte Mitgliedschaft für alle LIFTED Studios.

- Team Spirit: Regelmäßige Teamevents wie Padel, BBQs, Trainer Partys und mehr.

Du willst lernen, wie man ein Team für ein schnell wachsendes Startup aufbaut?

Dann ist das deine Chance: Wir sind ein hoch motiviertes Team mit einem schnell wachsenden, profitablen Geschäftsmodell und einer Mission mit echtem Purpose – Krafttraining für alle zugänglich zu machen. 

Wir schätzen deine Zeit genauso wie dein Talent . Deshalb kannst du auf ein klassisches Anschreiben verzichten. Schick uns einfach deinen CV und eine kurze Notiz (3–5 Sätze) , in der du dein relevantestes Achievement beschreibst.

Perks and Benefits

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

About the Role 

We are looking for a Director of Engineering to lead the Frontend Technologies domain within Marketplace. In this role, your mission will be two-fold: 

- Pivot our frontend setup for bigger efficiency : we have been operating in mostly the same frontend setup for at least 6 years, and recognize that change is imminent.

- Drive strategic engineering initiatives : architect and implement platform-specific changes that enhance modularity, autonomy, resilience, and performance across Android, iOS, and Web.

You will lead 4 Engineering Managers and 3 Staff Engineers and set and implement the FE strategy, which will impact the roadmaps of 9 Product domains within the Marketplace.

In this position, you will 

Strategically: 

- Ensure the most effective frontend setup for the Marketplace. We have 40+ teams, each with 3 frontend engineers (iOS, Android, and Web) in the Marketplace unit. We know this will look different in two years. Deciding what different means, and getting 9 product domains to fund it, is the job

- Drive Technology Strategy: Set and drive the future technology strategy for frontends, establishing a modular, scalable architecture that enables rapid development and strategic growth. Basically - raise the technological bar for all Marketplace unit. 

- Refine the domain's identity: Take sole ownership of shaping its future, successfully integrating Design Systems and engineering to treat our frontend platforms as a cohesive product.

Tactically : 

- Lead frontends: Lead a horizontal, platform-focused domain containing Android, iOS, Web, and Design System teams.

- Lead Initiatives: Oversee Marketplace-wide technical tooling, core libraries, and frameworks. Lead strategic projects, i.e., frontend modularization and modernization (SwiftUI/Jetpack Compose), native automated testing.

- Elevate global UI quality: Integrate design systems and accessibility into the frontend ecosystem to consolidate technical, visual and interaction quality standards. Support UI experimentation.

- Ensure Resilience & Reliability: Maintain robust release processes, Marketplace frontend quality, and performance monitoring to reduce downtime and ensure a consistent member experience.

- Innovate & Optimize: Drive AI-efficiency enablement in frontend development and explore cross-platform frontend development opportunities to increase engineering speed and productivity.

A lot of this work will be influencing without formal authority : Champion the frontend technical vision among your director peers, influencing the leaders of 9 Product domains to accommodate and prioritize platform-wide changes across 40+ teams.

About you 

How much of a technical acumen? Enough to have in depth conversations with our direct reports. You will have 4 strong technical EMs reporting to you, as well as 3 world-class staff engineers. We don’t think you need to match their technical competencies (that’s a stretch!), but you have to be able to speak their language, understand problems at their essence, and be able to consolidate and multiply their inputs, including being able to disagree objectively.

Leadership: you have a track record of making level change in the organizations that you lead (rather than 20% change). Consolidating your team views and making coherent strategy out of those views is step one. Step two is even more important: being able to implement these changes in your domain, and more so - across other domains in the marketplace - is a foundational ability you carry. In practice, that means you have at least 2 years of experience leading leaders and 5 years of experience influencing without authority. 

Change horizon: You are comfortable holding two timeframes at once. We need someone who can say, "Here is what our frontend setup should look like in two years, and here is why" AND name the clear deliverable that has to ship in the first quarter to make that end state reachable. Leaders who only do the second are common. Leaders who only do the first are entertaining. We need both.

What this role is not: This is not a hands-on frontend or release-engineering role. You will not be tuning CI, owning the release train, or reviewing architecture decisions yourself — you’ll have 4 strong EMs and 3 Staff Engineers close to the details, and your job is to turn their technical judgment into direction, alignment, and organizational change. - Experience with efficient training and model compression techniques, such as low-rank methods, quantisation, distillation, or sparsity.

- Strong Python skills and solid software-engineering practice, with experience on GPU and HPC environments and distributed training.

Preferred

- Knowledge of tensor networks and related numerical and optimisation

- Domain exposure to one or more of: finance, chemistry, or operations

The Rewards 

We are an international team of quantum technology experts and dedicated business creatives that are working to bring quantum-enabled solutions to the global market. Our brilliant team members enjoy a high degree of freedom working remotely or joining one of our office spaces. We have a vibrant, enthusiastic, passionate and creative culture driven by trust, excellence and continuous improvement. If you join the Terra Quantum team, you can expect:

- A competitive salary

Company description 

Quantum technologies have the potential to solve some of the world’s biggest challenges. There have been great advances in all areas of quantum technologies, and new fields of application are opened up every day. Hybrid computer systems that combine classic high-performance computing with quantum computers are already being used to develop solutions in sectors such as logistics, healthcare, finance, energy, automotive and aerospace. Quantum mechanical predictions are also used to obtain unprecedented precision in measurements, generate unbreakable codes, and form the basis of impenetrable communication networks. Quantum physics has, in some respects, parallels to the machine language of our computers-the zeros and ones into which our keyboard or touchscreen instructions are translated for execution in the computer-only on a larger scale: it is the machine language of the universe. The second quantum revolution is based on the control of individual quantum systems, such as individual atoms. We use quantum computers to solve currently unsolvable problems, simulate molecules and their interactions, find drugs for diseases that are not yet curable, find new materials, or make artificial intelligence stronger. Quantum is now. 

Terra Quantum is a future-focused quantum services and technology company working on making the second quantum revolution a reality. Terra Quantum’s activities span all areas, markets, and industries globally.

title: 2027 NextGen Talent Operations Programme
description:
Company Description 

We’re Checkout.com . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. 

We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. 

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. 

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. 

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. 

The role 

We are seeking an exceptionally organized, tech-forward Talent Operations Associate to join our Global Talent Acquisition team. As our Talent Operations Associate in London , you will bridge the gap between ensuring our recruiters, and interviewer community are able to find the best talent, through cutting-edge Talent Operations.

We are seeking a proactive AI and automation expert to transform our hiring operations. In this role, you will leverage emerging tools to streamline scheduling, resolve logistics challenges, and build data-driven dashboards. If you thrive on solving complex problems, engaging consultatively with senior stakeholders, and redefining talent operations, we want to hear from you.

description:
This an Atlantic portfolio venture. 

About the Venture 

This early-stage venture is building a discovery engine for chemistry, comprising a platform for running end-to-end simulations of chemical reaction systems, and a world model + agent stack that uses the simulation platform to discover new chemistry.

Their goal is to build backend scientific data infrastructure to meet the demands of AI systems that can truly accelerate and automate the discovery layer of chemistry.

Both founders hold PhDs in Chemistry from the University of Oxford, and the venture has already secured pre-seed funding. They are now building out their founding team.

The Role 

- As a Computational Chemist, you will play a central role in shaping the scientific foundations of the venture's technology, helping develop the computational methods and workflows that underpin its end-to-end chemical reaction simulation platform.

- You’ll work closely with researchers and engineers to integrate state-of-the-art computational chemistry methods with machine learning approaches, driving progress towards the venture's strategic and scientific objectives.

- You’ll take ownership of developing, validating and optimising the computational chemistry components of the platform, with a particular focus on reaction mechanisms, reaction kinetics, molecular dynamics and the modelling of complex chemical environments.

- You will design, implement and refine scalable scientific workflows for generating, processing and analysing chemical reaction data, improving the accuracy, reliability and computational efficiency of simulations.

- Beyond your core scientific responsibilities, the team is looking for someone who can contribute to strategic research decisions, bring strong independent scientific judgement, and help shape the interdisciplinary research culture of the company at an early stage.

What You'll Work On 

- Foundation models for chemical reactivity: The team is building and training foundation models for chemical reactivity with a variety of data modalities. You'll help curate this foundational data corpus by developing cheminformatics and computational chemistry workflows for generating data from combinatorial enumeration, as well as robust data filtering, clustering and validation routines.

- Computational methods: The team is working on efficient computational methods from which foundational data is generated and the platform is validated. You'll be responsible for developing protocols for estimating solvation and entropy factors in chemical reaction steps. This involves keeping up to date with published literature for ideas and inspiration.

- Generative models: The venture is expanding its foundational data corpus beyond combinatorial workflows. You'll help design, validate and benchmark the generative model architectures that accomplish this.

- Chemical reaction simulation: The team is building out an end-to-end chemical reaction simulation platform. You'll be involved in designing the architecture and assembling the platform, as well as developing benchmarks and validation protocols against computational and experimental methods.

- World models and agents: The venture will be developing an agent + world model stack that operates on the simulation platform. You'll be responsible for formulating the action space in which the world model is trained and the agent explores new chemical reaction space.

What They're Looking For 

The team is looking for someone who enjoys being given a blank canvas and the chance to create something spectacular with it. In particular, someone who brings:

- A PhD in Computational Chemistry, Machine Learning, or a related field.

- Intellectual curiosity: Someone who enjoys venturing outside their comfort zone, exploring new ideas and applying their knowledge and experience to unfamiliar domains.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Data Enrichment Platform
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Data Enrichment Platform Team 

Our Enrichment Orchestration team builds the platform that enables Wayve’s teams to deploy, run, evaluate and continually improve machine-learning models. Processing petabytes of driving data across large GPU fleets, the team creates dependable, self-service capabilities that help model engineers understand model performance, improve quality and reduce operational effort and cost.

As our Staff Software Engineer, you’ll own the platform’s technical vision and long-term direction. You’ll combine hands-on engineering with cross-team technical leadership, shaping how model engineering, infrastructure, compute and data capabilities come together to accelerate model development.

🧠 Your day-to-day 

- Own the technical vision and architecture for the end-to-end Data Enrichment Platform, translating user needs into a clear technical direction.

- Lead the design, development and operation of backend services, APIs, model-execution workflows, versioned outputs, annotation capabilities and dataset catalogues.

- Make architectural decisions for petabyte-scale data and large GPU fleets, addressing data locality, scheduling, capacity, backpressure, failure recovery, observability and cost.

- Evaluate when to build, buy, reuse, integrate, consolidate or replace technologies as Wayve’s needs and the technology landscape evolve.

- Establish clear technical boundaries and ownership across model engineering, AI Platform, infrastructure, compute, storage and data teams.

- Remain hands-on while leading cross-team delivery, mentoring senior engineers and raising standards for maintainable, tested and observable software.

- Drive adoption of reusable, self-service capabilities so teams can onboard and operate workflows independently.

- Define measurable service levels and success metrics covering reliability, throughput, cost, automation and adoption.

🧩 What you’ll be working on 

- A scalable platform for large-scale inference, automated evaluation, model monitoring, active learning and retraining.

- Self-service backend services and APIs that enable dozens of model engineers to deploy and operate repeatable workflows independently.

- Reproducible dataset selection, versioned outputs, annotation workflows and dataset catalogues with clear metadata, provenance and lineage.

- Reliable model-execution workflows operating across petabytes of driving data and large GPU fleets, scaling towards thousands of GPUs.

- Monitoring and operational tooling that make model quality, platform reliability, throughput, cost, runtime and workflow status visible.

- The foundations for continuous evaluation, drift detection and automated model-improvement loops across robotics and computer-vision workloads.

- Architectural improvements that reduce inference costs, duplicate compute and manual operational effort.

🙌 You should apply if 

- You have owned the long-term technical direction of a complex, multi-system platform or capability and can demonstrate the measurable outcomes of your decisions.

- You have strong production software-engineering experience in Python, building maintainable, tested and observable backend services, APIs and data-processing systems.

- You have deep experience designing and operating large-scale distributed systems for data-intensive or compute-intensive workloads.

- You have a track record of turning internal platforms into widely adopted, reliable and usable self-service products.

- You bring excellent architecture and technology judgement, balancing immediate delivery needs with long-term platform direction.

- You remain hands-on while leading delivery across organisational boundaries, influencing technical decisions and aligning teams around clear ownership and shared outcomes.

- You communicate complex ideas clearly and have experience mentoring senior engineers and strengthening the technical capabilities of those around you.

- Experience with workflow orchestration, batch inference, ML platforms, model deployment or registries would be an advantage. Relevant technologies include Flyte, Airflow, Dagster, Argo, Spark, Databricks, Ray, Kubernetes and GPU infrastructure.

- Experience with annotation or dataset-catalogue platforms, including provenance, versioning, lineage and quality control, would also be valuable.

- Experience with production robotics or computer-vision platforms—including annotation, inference, evaluation and model monitoring—is particularly desirable. Computer-vision research expertise is not required.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! 

If you’re passionate about autonomy and the impact you could make at Wayve, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve 

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end-to-end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real-world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand-coded rules or pre-mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once-in-a-generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human-driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware-agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2+ through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real-world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻 — Locations & Flexible Working 

This role is based in London. Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process 

Our process is clear and respectful of your time.

Initial call / Talent Partner screen (30 mins)

Competency interviews: Python coding (60 mins), System design (60 mins)

Deep Dive Interviews: Technical Leadership, Hiring Manager interview (45 mins)

Final interview: Mission, values and Staff-level calibration (45 mins)

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (location dependent) 

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually

📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long-term success of Wayve

✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable

✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands-on in vehicle workshops and labs

📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth

🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

title: Quantitative Researcher - 2027 Graduates
description:
At Graviton, we don't believe the best trading strategies come from following established playbooks. They come from asking better questions. Why does a pattern exist? What is driving it? Is it real or just noise? Can it be explained, modelled and turned into an edge?

As a Quantitative Researcher, you'll work on those questions every day. You'll investigate market behaviour, develop quantitative models, build and test hypotheses and turn insights into trading strategies, working alongside researchers and technologists in an environment where an idea on a whiteboard can reach live trading quickly.

This isn't a role where the answers are in a textbook. The problems are open-ended, the data is enormous, and finding the answers is the job.

Ideal candidates are rigorous thinkers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious, based in our Singapore, London, Amsterdam or US offices.

What You'll Work On

You'll work across quantitative research and systematic trading, taking ideas through the full lifecycle: question, hypothesis, experiment, model, validation, strategy, production. Depending on your team and research interests, your work would include:

- Discovering predictive patterns and sources of alpha from billions of market events

- Formulating hypotheses about market behaviour and designing experiments to test them

- Applying probability, statistics, optimization and machine learning to build predictive models and quantitative signals for systematic trading

- Designing robust backtests and statistical tests to distinguish genuine signals from noise

- Working with large and complex datasets to uncover patterns that aren't immediately visible

- Investigating market microstructure and how markets behave at different timescales

- Evaluating strategy performance, identifying weaknesses and continuously refining models

- Developing research infrastructure and AI-powered tools and agents that make experimentation faster and analysis deeper

- Working closely with technologists to translate research ideas into efficient, production-ready systems

- Exploring new techniques in machine learning, statistics and quantitative finance to uncover new sources of edge

No two research problems are the same. Good research finds patterns. Great research understands why they exist.

What Success Looks Like

Successful researchers at Graviton discover new sources of alpha and turn them into robust trading strategies, build models that hold up under real market conditions and not only in backtests, develop a deep understanding of market behaviour, create research frameworks and tools that make the broader team more effective, work with technologists to take ideas from research into production, and communicate complex quantitative ideas clearly and rigorously. Your impact isn't measured by how many models you build. It's measured by the quality of the ideas you discover and what those ideas enable.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for exceptional problem solvers who genuinely enjoy mathematics, programming and figuring out things that aren't obvious.

- Degree in a quantitative discipline such as mathematics, physics, computer science, statistics, operations research or machine learning

- No active backlogs

- Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++

- Solid grounding in probability, statistics, linear algebra and optimization, with experience in machine learning, statistical modelling or data analysis, whether through coursework, research or personal projects

- Comfort working with large, complex datasets, and strong analytical thinking

- A passion for applying quantitative thinking and rigorous research to solve open-ended problems in markets

- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly

Prior exposure to quantitative research, algorithmic trading, market microstructure, competitive mathematics or machine learning is valuable, but we care more about how you think than whether you've worked in finance before.

Our Culture

More than specific tools or techniques, we care how you think. We look for people who are curious enough to keep asking why, analytical enough to separate signal from noise, persistent enough to pursue difficult problems, intellectually honest enough to abandon an idea when the evidence says so, and humble enough to keep learning.

At Graviton, researchers sit alongside technologists on specialized trading teams that operate with significant autonomy. You'll have meaningful ownership of research problems from day one: forming your own hypotheses, challenging existing approaches and following the evidence wherever it leads, with the infrastructure and datasets to test ideas at scale, competitive compensation, and a culture where the best idea wins regardless of who proposed it.

Markets are among the most complex systems humans have ever created, and they never stop changing. Neither should our thinking. Every day, someone asks a better question and finds an answer nobody had. That someone could be you.

At Swap, we’re building a culture that values clarity, creativity, and shared ownership as we redefine how global commerce works.

About the role 

Our agentic storefront is an AI shopping experience that helps shoppers discover, decide, and buy through natural conversation.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you’ll be a technical leader on the team building it. You’ll set direction for several engineering teams, take on the hardest cross-cutting problems, and stay hands-on in the code that matters most. You’ll work closely with Product, Design, Data, and engineering leadership to turn ambitious goals into practical plans, and you’ll help the engineers around you do their best work.

Responsibilities 

- Lead large initiatives that run for several quarters and involve multiple teams, from first scoping through to production.

- Write exemplar code in critical paths, setting the implementation bar for the wider group.

- Review important designs from other teams, helping engineers balance quality, speed, reliability, and long-term maintainability.

- Define and uphold operational standards for the group: monitoring, availability, scalability, security, release safety, and cost awareness. Help lead serious incidents and follow through on the right fixes.

- Lead tool evaluations and architecture migrations, making build-vs-buy trade-offs explicit.

- Use AI well beyond the basics, and push back on AI-generated complexity so code health holds as we speed up.

- Own the business result of your work. Define success metrics, monitor after launch, and challenge constructively when something won’t move the needle for merchants.

- Mentor Senior Engineers and below, and lead or join senior-level interviews.

- Write and improve the documentation others rely on, such as architecture direction, decision records, and runbooks.

Requirements 

- Significant experience (typically 8+ years) building and shipping production software, with a record of leading complex initiatives that cross team lines.

- Deep expertise in TypeScript/JavaScript and Node.js, including architecting REST and/or GraphQL APIs and distributed systems.

- Comfort outside your home language and stack. We expect Staff engineers to be T-shaped.

- Strong relational database, data modelling, and SQL skills, plus familiarity with NoSQL.

- Experience designing for reliability and scale in the cloud, with solid CI/CD, observability, and incident-response practices.

- Hands-on experience with LLMs or agentic systems, or a track record of picking up new technology fast and applying it sensibly.

- Daily use of AI coding tools, with a sense for when to trust them and when not to.

- Experience in eCommerce systems and platforms is preferred.

- Excellent written and verbal communication. You can explain trade-offs in business terms to any audience.

- A team player with a bias for ownership: you bring a solution along with the problem, and work isn’t done until it’s live and stable.

What we offer

title: Quality Systems Lead
description:
About us 

Encord is the universal data layer for AI that helps 300+ AI teams train and run models on the right data. Our platform indexes, curates, annotates, and evaluates data across the full AI lifecycle, from development through production.

Trusted by Woven by Toyota, AXA, UiPath, Zipline, and more. We're an ambitious team of 100+ working at the frontier of AI and have raised $60M in Series C funding from Wellington Management, CRV, Next47 and Y Combinator.

The role 

We're hiring a Quality Systems Lead to own how Encord measures the quality of the human data we deliver to frontier AI labs, physical AI companies and enterprise AI teams — the standard itself, the systems that evaluate against it, and the audit function that produces the ground truth behind both. Data quality is what our customers buy. As we scale across data types — image and video, document, medical, LLM evaluation, robot teleoperation, egocentric capture — quality coverage cannot scale linearly with headcount. So this role has two halves that make each other work. You will build automated evaluation: model-assisted and LLM-based screening, agreement analysis at scale, anomaly and drift detection across annotation output. And you will build and run a dedicated audit team of around ten specialists in India, whose judgements become the labelled ground truth that trains and calibrates that automated layer. As coverage automates, the audit team moves up to the cases models can't judge and to generating gold sets for each new data type we take on. It is an unusual combination — engineering and consistent QC operations in one person — and it is the combination the job needs. You will also have an advantage your counterparts elsewhere in the industry don't: Encord owns the platform this work runs on, so the measurement you build can become native capability in the product rather than internal tooling.

What you'll do 

- Build automated dataset quality evaluation and root-cause detection — model-assisted and LLM-as-judge screening, agreement analysis at scale, anomaly and drift detection across annotation output

- Hire, train, calibrate and manage a dedicated audit team of around ten specialists based in our India operation, held to inter-rater agreement and catch rate rather than volume audited

- Turn audit output into labelled ground truth that trains and validates the automated layer, and manage the ratio of automated to manual coverage deliberately over time

- Own the quality standard for every data type we deliver — written rubrics with worked edge cases, golden sets, and acceptance criteria agreed with the customer, alongside the Special Projects lead, before the first batch ships

- Build scoring systems that rank annotator and reviewer performance and feed routing, staffing and offboarding decisions

- Set the pass thresholds that certification gates on, so nobody works a project queue without having demonstrated they meet the standard

- Report quality KPIs to leadership, and into the reporting our Special Projects leads take to customers: accuracy against client spec, inter-annotator agreement, rework rate, cost of rework, and coverage

- Work with Project Management on remediation — you produce the measurement and the diagnosis, production owns fixing the project, and the standard stays independent of the people being measured

- Own the unit economics of quality: cost per audited unit, and the coverage you buy per pound spent

- Partner with Product and Engineering to bring quality measurement into Encord platform as native capability

Who we're looking for 

- You build and you operate. You'll write the evaluation pipeline, and you'll also run the weekly calibration session with ten auditors in another country

- Your instinct on a coverage problem is to automate it — you reach for a model, a heuristic or a better sampling design before you reach for more auditors

- Statistically literate in a practical way: sampling design, agreement statistics, and the judgement to spot a metric being optimised against rather than met

- You can hold a calibrated standard across a distributed team you don't sit with — you know that ten uncalibrated auditors produce ten standards

- A strong writer. Much of this job is producing rubrics a distributed workforce can follow without you in the room

- You hold a standard under commercial pressure, and you bring the evidence that makes it stick with a delivery team or a client

- Systems thinker: as interested in why a failure recurs across projects as in this project's defect rate

Experience requirements 

- 4+ years owning both technical and operational outcomes in a data, AI or service delivery environment where quality was measured rather than asserted

- Hands-on Python and SQL. You build the analysis and the tooling rather than specify it for someone else

- Practical experience applying models to a quality or evaluation problem — LLM-as-judge, model-assisted QA, automated evaluation, anomaly detection or classifier-based screening

- Sampling methodology and agreement statistics (Cohen's and Fleiss' kappa, F1 against ground truth) applied to real production data

- Experience hiring, training and managing a team, ideally an audit, review or QA team, and ideally distributed

- Track record of building a quality framework or function, including the reporting leadership and customers run on

- Bonus: direct experience of annotation, evaluation or model-training workflows, and of what frontier AI labs accept as evidence of quality

- Bonus: a STEM degree, or a background in data science or research engineering

- Bonus: multilingual delivery and linguistic quality assessment

Why Encord

- 25 days annual leave + UK public holidays

- Annual learning & development budget

- Fluency in evaluation: designing datasets and quality metrics (such as AUC, NDCG, precision and recall), and using LLM-as-a-judge and human feedback.

title: Senior Consumer Duty Specialist
description:
About Pleo 

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role 

In this role, you will play a central part in assessing, questioning, and enhancing how customers experience Pleo. Drawing on deep regulatory knowledge, you will lead Consumer Duty initiatives, actively spot potential customer harm, examine what drives customer journeys, and ensure targeted remediation creates lasting, positive impact.

You'll need sharp analytical skills and the confidence to influence stakeholders, translating data and MI into decisive action. You will construct and manage dashboards and reporting mechanisms that illuminate emerging patterns, vulnerable customer risks, and key concerns, offering executive leadership clear visibility into operational gaps and necessary solutions.

Your contribution goes well beyond producing MI. You will conduct QA across complex complaint handling and sensitive customer interactions, manage Ombudsman cases, and speak up when evidence shows outcomes aren't meeting expectations. Collaborating across teams, you'll turn data-driven insights into practical improvements, drive projects to completion, and evaluate whether changes deliver real results for our users.

We're seeking someone who views Consumer Duty as a powerful driver of business improvement rather than a routine compliance exercise. You'll bring together technical understanding, rigorous analysis, and constructive challenge to investigate root causes, align key partners, deliver change, and prove that customer experiences are continuously getting better.

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to 

You'll work closely with teams across Customer Support, Complaints, Compliance, Risk, Operations, Product, Data, Technology, and other business functions.

The role will have broad exposure across the organisation, particularly when customer outcome risks or Consumer Duty-related remediation require cross-functional action.

You'll also work closely with senior stakeholders through Consumer Duty governance and reporting, helping translate detailed analysis into clear insights, risks, recommendations, and actions.

What you’ll be doing 

As a Consumer Duty Specialist, you will:

- Turn data into customer outcome insight : Build and own MI, dashboards, KPIs, and reporting that give the business a clear view of customer outcomes, trends, risks, and emerging areas of concern.

- Own Consumer Duty reporting : Produce monthly and quarterly Consumer Duty reporting, turning complex data into a clear story for senior leadership and Board-level audiences. You'll go beyond showing what happened to explain why it matters and what we should do about it .

- Identify customer harm : Use complaints, QA findings, customer feedback, vulnerable customer data, Ombudsman cases, and MI to identify potential customer harm, emerging risks, and systemic issues.

- Challenge the business : Where the evidence suggests customers aren't receiving good outcomes, you'll be expected to ask difficult questions, challenge assumptions, and ensure the issue is properly understood and addressed.

- Drive remediation and change : Work with stakeholders across the business to agree remediation plans, establish clear owners and timelines, and help drive Consumer Duty-related projects and improvements through to completion.

- Provide complaints QA : Conduct weekly quality reviews of complaints handled by the Complaints Manager, using findings to identify quality issues, customer risks, and wider trends.

- Manage Ombudsman activity : Act as the primary operational contact with the UK Ombudsman, managing referred complaints, responses, remedies, compensation, invoices, and related communications.

- Leverage AI and smart automation : Spot opportunities to apply automated tools and AI to scale and streamline Consumer Duty analytics, monitoring, and workflows. You will feel empowered to test emerging tech and eliminate repetitive manual work, maintaining proper critical evaluation and human governance whenever compliance risks or customer impacts are involved.

What you bring 

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

- Strong Consumer Duty knowledge : You understand the principles of Consumer Duty and how they translate into practical customer outcomes, particularly across complaints, customer support, vulnerable customers, and customer journeys.

- Strong data and MI experience : You know how to take complex data, build meaningful dashboards and reporting, and identify the insights that actually matter. You're comfortable working with data rather than simply consuming reports created by others.

- A customer outcome mindset : You're naturally curious about how customers are experiencing the business and are able to connect data, customer feedback, complaints, and operational activity to real customer outcomes.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills : You can spot trends, anomalies, and patterns, investigate root causes, and determine whether an issue is isolated or potentially systemic.

- The confidence to challenge : You're comfortable questioning decisions, processes, and assumptions when the evidence suggests customers may be experiencing poor outcomes. You can challenge constructively and build relationships at the same time.

- A bias towards action : You don't believe reporting is the end of the process. You want to understand what needs to change, bring people together, and help make it happen.

- Project and remediation experience : You're comfortable managing actions, timelines, dependencies, stakeholders, and risks across cross-functional projects, particularly where there is a regulatory, customer, or operational outcome to deliver.

- An AI and automation mindset : You're naturally curious about how AI and automation can make processes more efficient, improve analysis, and free up time for higher-value work. You look for sensible opportunities to automate repetitive tasks and use AI to augment your thinking, while maintaining appropriate human oversight, critical judgement, and accountability — particularly where customer outcomes or regulatory decisions are involved.

Why is this role a good fit for you 

This role is a good fit for you if:

- You love using data to uncover things that others might not see.

- You want your analysis to drive real change, rather than sit in a report or dashboard.

- You enjoy asking "why?" and getting to the root cause of customer problems.

- You're comfortable challenging the business when the evidence tells you something isn't working.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

- You prefer to produce reporting without being involved in what happens afterwards.

- You're uncomfortable challenging stakeholders or having difficult conversations when customer outcomes aren't where they should be.

- You prefer working within a narrow functional remit rather than across multiple teams.

How you’ll develop in this role 

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you'll:

- Build a deep understanding of our customer outcome data, existing Consumer Duty MI, complaints, vulnerable customer journeys, and current areas of risk.

- Take ownership of key Consumer Duty dashboards and reporting, developing a clear view of the metrics and insights that matter most.

- Establish strong relationships with stakeholders across Customer Support, Complaints, Compliance, Risk, Operations, Product, Data, and Technology.

- Lead the analysis behind Consumer Duty reporting and help shape how customer outcomes are presented to senior stakeholders and the Board.

Over time, you'll have the opportunity to shape how Pleo measures, understands, and improves customer outcomes, helping move Consumer Duty from a regulatory obligation into a genuine driver of better customer experiences and better business decisions.

Show me the benefits! 

- Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

- Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

- Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

- We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays

- For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

- Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice

- We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

- Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

The interview process 

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

- Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

- Meet the Hiring Manager: 1hr going through role in more depth.

- Pleo Challenge: A case study were you talk us through how you'd solve a work appropriate challenge.

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we advertised this role, we received a really high volume of applications but could only select so many. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:

- CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

- Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

- Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.

title: Senior Engagement Manager
description:

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.
